subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose host IPC for Docker sandboxes, and if yes should it be a narrow explicit `sandbox.docker.ipc` break-glass field instead of raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: Source inspection shows GPU support is already implemented and shipped, while the remaining host IPC/raw-args request changes the sandbox isolation boundary and config contract.

options.title: Add narrow host IPC field
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, create-args, security-audit coverage, and warnings, while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

options.title: Reject host IPC in core
options.body: Document that host IPC weakens sandbox isolation and keep GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path.

options.title: Design broader namespace policy
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a consistent policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add narrow host IPC field
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, create-args, security-audit coverage, and warnings, while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest individual history match for recent sandbox namespace hardening and CODEOWNERS-sensitive security paths.
